description: §14.8.9 — declassification is COLUMN-keyed, not existence-keyed. `passwordHash` is the protected column; the body reveals `email`. That reveal declassifies nothing about `passwordHash`, so the raw-egress gate still fires E-PROTECT-004. The adversarial twin of `reveal-suppresses-e004`, which reveals the RIGHT column and is correctly silent.
rationale: §14.8.9: `reveal("col")` stamps THE NAMED COLUMN's provenance descriptor as declassified-at-this-value — it is a per-column admit, not a per-body switch. Until S405 the gate's suppression tested only for the PRESENCE of a `.reveal(` anywhere in the body, so revealing any column disarmed the gate for every protected column in that body: `reveal("email")` silently declassified `passwordHash`. This case pins the narrowed rule — the gate is discharged only when every protected OUTPUT column of the offending query is named by a reveal. It goes red against the pre-S405 emitter, which is what makes it a proof rather than a description.
